evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: adults in randomized trials of whole oats or isolated oat beta-glucan assessing lipid outcomes
evidence.supported_claim_language: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 28 randomized studies found that whole oats and isolated oat beta-glucan reduced total and LDL cholesterol, while isolated beta-glucan also reduced triglycerides. HDL cholesterol was not significantly changed. Food-matrix and isolated-fiber evidence should remain distinct rather than treated as one identical exposure.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.safety_note: Beta-glucan source, processing, viscosity, dose, and food matrix can affect results. Pooled lipid effects do not establish treatment equivalence with lipid-lowering medication.

evidence.effect_or_condition: body weight in overweight and obesity
evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
evidence.population: overweight or obese adults receiving glucomannan or placebo
evidence.supported_claim_language: A meta-analysis of randomized trials found no statistically significant reduction in body weight with glucomannan versus placebo; the pooled mean difference was about -0.22 kg and heterogeneity was substantial. This does not support presenting glucomannan as a reliable stand-alone weight-loss intervention.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; null pooled weight-loss effect
evidence.safety_note: Gastrointestinal adverse effects were reported in the trial literature. As a highly absorbent fiber, glucomannan also requires appropriate administration and medication-separation context.

evidence.effect_or_condition: body composition and muscle strength during resistance training in older adults
evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: adults aged 50 years or older participating in resistance training
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2026 meta-analysis of 13 randomized trials found that adding HMB to resistance training in adults aged 50 years or older did not significantly improve fat mass, muscle mass, or muscle strength compared with resistance training without HMB. The result argues against treating HMB as a routine performance adjunct in this population.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials; largely null adjunctive evidence
evidence.safety_note: These findings apply to older adults already performing resistance training and should not be generalized to bed rest, severe frailty, cachexia, or other clinical settings with different physiology and baseline risk.

evidence.study_type: systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: adults in randomized artichoke supplementation trials assessing lipid outcomes
evidence.supported_claim_language: A systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis found pooled reductions in triglycerides, total cholesterol, and LDL cholesterol with artichoke supplementation, while HDL cholesterol was not significantly increased. Preparations and baseline metabolic status varied across studies, so the evidence is best framed as a modest biomarker signal.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of randomized trials
evidence.safety_note: Artichoke extracts and juices are not interchangeable, and pooled lipid changes do not establish cardiovascular-event benefit or treatment equivalence with lipid-lowering medicines.

evidence.study_type: systematic review of randomized clinical trials
evidence.population: adults in randomized maca trials assessing sexual function or desire
evidence.supported_claim_language: A systematic review identified four randomized maca trials; some reported favorable sexual-function or desire outcomes, while another found no significant benefit. The evidence base was too small and methodologically limited for firm conclusions.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review; limited evidence from few small trials
evidence.safety_note: Maca preparations, populations, and outcomes differed across studies. Limited positive signals should not be promoted as established treatment for sexual dysfunction or infertility.

evidence.population: adults in randomized DHEA supplementation trials
evidence.supported_claim_language: A meta-analysis of randomized trials found small pooled increases in lean body mass and decreases in fat mass with DHEA, while body weight, BMI, systolic blood pressure, and diastolic blood pressure were not significantly changed. Whether the small body-composition shifts translate into meaningful clinical benefit remains uncertain.
evidence.evidence_grade: meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials; small body-composition effects
evidence.safety_note: DHEA is a hormonal precursor rather than a neutral wellness nutrient. Hormone-sensitive conditions, endocrine effects, drug interactions, age, sex, and product quality materially affect safety and interpretation.

evidence.study_type: review of human Cordyceps supplementation studies
evidence.population: mostly young or physically active adults in human exercise studies
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2025 review of human Cordyceps studies found some signals for improved time to exhaustion after multiweek supplementation, while effects on aerobic-fitness measures were inconsistent. Small samples, varied preparations, and combination products limit confidence in a broad ergogenic claim.
evidence.evidence_grade: human evidence review; limited and heterogeneous
evidence.safety_note: Cordyceps species, cultivated products, extracts, and multi-ingredient formulas are not interchangeable. Combination-product results should not be attributed to Cordyceps alone.

evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical trials
evidence.population: men in clinical trials of Eurycoma longifolia, including men with and without hypogonadism
evidence.sample_size: 9 studies in systematic review; 5 randomized controlled trials in meta-analysis
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2022 systematic review and meta-analysis found a pooled increase in total testosterone with Eurycoma longifolia, with a clearer signal in men with hypogonadism. Testosterone is a biomarker, however, and the analysis does not establish consistent improvements in symptoms, fertility, strength, or other functional outcomes.
evidence.safety_note: Extract standardization and product identity vary substantially. Hormonal effects, underlying causes of low testosterone, medication use, and long-term safety require clinical context.

evidence.study_type: GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: adults in randomized Moringa oleifera supplementation trials
evidence.sample_size: 9 randomized controlled trials; 12 intervention arms; 341 intervention and 308 control participants
evidence.supported_claim_language: A 2025 GRADE-assessed meta-analysis found no consistent improvement in most cardiometabolic outcomes with Moringa oleifera. A modest diastolic-blood-pressure signal was not robust in sensitivity analysis, and overall certainty was rated very low.
evidence.evidence_grade: GRADE-assessed systematic review/meta-analysis; very-low certainty and largely null evidence
evidence.safety_note: Moringa leaf powders, extracts, preparations, doses, and populations differed across trials. The evidence does not support using Moringa as a substitute for established blood-pressure, lipid, or glucose treatment.

evidence.effect_or_condition: depressive symptoms as adjunctive or stand-alone treatment
evidence.study_type: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
evidence.population: people with depressive disorders receiving folate alone or added to other treatment
evidence.supported_claim_language: A systematic review of three randomized trials found a modest reduction in depression rating scores when folate was added to other treatment, while a small comparison of folate alone versus trazodone did not show a significant difference. The evidence was limited and did not establish which patients benefit most or whether baseline folate status modifies response.
evidence.evidence_grade: systematic review/meta-analysis; limited evidence from three small trials
evidence.safety_note: Folic acid, folinic acid, and L-methylfolate are not equivalent interventions. Folate supplementation can also mask hematologic signs of vitamin B12 deficiency, so adjunctive psychiatric evidence should not be converted into unsupervised treatment advice.
